label: first occurrence of b/d/h/r/i/o/p/m at original positions 2-6
explanation: Fires only in the original-input phase (never at <DEL> or during copy), mostly at positions 3-5 (none at t=0, rare at t=1 or t>=7). Driven by the current input token: b is by far the strongest (35% of mass, 9x lift), then d, h, r, i, o, p, m; a, digits 0/3 and most other tokens rarely fire. 94% of mass is on the first occurrence of the token. Magnitude is higher when earlier tokens come from {1, t, w, y, v, c, n, z, x} (e.g. top examples start 1 1 ... b), and lower or absent when earlier inputs include other trigger letters. The predicate captures ~87% of activation mass on dev but precision is only ~0.11: most matching steps stay below threshold, depending on prefix context in a way no simple history condition captured (best F1 ~0.30).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=2: b, d, h, r; t=1: b; t=3: b, d, h, r) and the first original token (most: 1, t, w, c, n, z; least: d, p, f, r); timing cues that raise it most: t=4, t=3, t=5.
